brief: How a tiny niche made me rich. The 1,200-person market I built a $40k/month business in. Why niche is the new big in the AI era.

slots.stickyNote: here's how small beats big and pays better
slots.intro: I ignored every guru and built for a market most founders would laugh at. It changed everything.

slots.title: Big markets
slots.subtitle: Everyone chases millions of users. I found riches where nobody else was looking.
slots.insight1Title: My total addressable market was 1,200 people
slots.insight1Body: That's it. No venture scale. Just a painful problem and a credit card.
slots.insight2Title: They paid more because options were scarce
slots.insight2Body: With no competition, I set the price. They said yes.
slots.insight3Body: One person can now serve a village at software speed.
slots.authorQuote: I stopped building for everyone and finally started winning.

slots.title: Speed beats
slots.subtitle: I shipped an ugly landing page in a weekend. It made $8k before I redesigned it.
slots.insight1Title: I launched with three features, not thirty
slots.insight1Body: The other twenty-seven were just procrastination dressed as product strategy.
slots.insight2Body: That embarrassment earned $40k while I waited for courage.
slots.insight3Body: They want the fix, not the font choice.
slots.authorQuote: Perfection is just fear in a nicer font.

slots.title: Small market
slots.subtitle: When you're the only specialist, you don't compete. You collect.
slots.insight1Title: I charged 10x what mass tools cost
slots.insight1Body: Enterprise budgets hide in the tiniest, most specific corners.
slots.insight2Body: If they found me, they already knew they needed it.
slots.insight3Body: Cash flow became my superpower on day one.
slots.authorQuote: The riches are in the niches everyone ignores.

slots.title: One person
slots.subtitle: I automated support, onboarding, and content. My margin stayed fat.
slots.insight1Title: AI wrote the docs I hated writing
slots.insight1Body: Suddenly a solo founder looked like a twenty-person team.
slots.insight2Body: I contacted every prospect in my niche in one afternoon.
slots.insight3Body: Every support ticket became a smarter feature without more headcount.
slots.authorQuote: AI didn't replace me. It made my niche unstoppable.

slots.title: Saying no
slots.subtitle: Enterprise requests almost pulled me out of the niche that built me.
slots.insight1Body: I quoted them triple. They said yes. I still said no.
slots.insight2Body: Every detour is a tax on the customers who love you.
slots.insight3Body: My bank account preferred the quiet recurring revenue instead.
slots.authorQuote: The hardest wins come from refusing the wrong yes.

slots.title: Find your
slots.subtitle: Stop validating. Start building for the weird problem only you see.
slots.insight1Body: That one weird complaint is a million-dollar niche in disguise.
slots.insight2Body: You can't validate a niche from a Google Doc.
slots.insight3Body: If your price doesn't sting, you're leaving money on the table.
slots.authorQuote: Your niche isn't too small. Your ambition is just too loud.

slots.ctaBody: If one founder skips the crowded market because of this, my job is done.
